- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  
  • Microgynon (combined OCP) – dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • Paracetamol – dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • Planned: Ibuprofen (per clinician advice) – dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • Allergy: Aspirin (causes marked nausea)  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  On combined OCP for 6 years; last menstrual period ~1 week ago; no contraception side-effects reported

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 24-hour history of unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia, no focal neurological deficits, afebrile by history, no prior headache history, family history of migraine, OCP use.

Working diagnosis: Migraine without aura  
• Supported by unilateral throbbing quality, photophobia, relief in dark, female with positive family history.  
• No red-flag features (sudden thunderclap, neurologic deficit, fever, neck stiffness).

Considerations:  
• Tension-type headache – work stress; less likely given throbbing quality and photophobia.  
• Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – low-medium likelihood due to OCP use; monitor for progression, neuro signs.

Management:  
• Start NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen) with ongoing Paracetamol; ensure adequate hydration.  
• Advise rest in dark room, monitor symptom changes.  
• Safety-net: seek urgent review for worsening pain, fever, rash, neurological changes, or new symptoms.  
• Arrange blood pressure check (clinic or community pharmacy) and obtain home thermometer.  
• Re-evaluate if headaches become recurrent or pattern suggests menstrual association; may consider migraine prophylaxis in future.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Discussed hydration, safe NSAID use, stress management, and importance of monitoring for red-flag symptoms  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Relief of current headache; return to work activities  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Planned BP check (local clinic/pharmacy); no other referrals at this stage  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Advise to contact clinic if headache worsens or persists; routine follow-up if symptoms recur  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Not recorded (may revisit if work stress persists)  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not indicated currently  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Migraine without aura – High likelihood: Unilateral throbbing pain, photophobia, family history, typical demographic, no neurologic deficits.  
2. Tension-type headache – Medium likelihood: Work stress and fluctuating pain, but photophobia and throbbing less typical.  
3. Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – Low-Medium likelihood: OCP use and new headache; currently lacks focal deficits or progression.
